gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-chivo: Tilt Neon is all tube and swagger, its stroke never changing width. Chivo packs its lowercase up toward the caps, with daylight in every curve, and handles the reading while the heading shouts.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-comme: Wire-bright and loud, Tilt Neon stretches its lowercase tall in a tube-like line, while Comme reads smooth with no clogged curves. Loud against smooth is the whole story here.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-cossette-texte: Tilt Neon draws bold tubes with a splayed c and short ascenders, made to grab attention. And Cossette Texte keeps the text moving, its wide-eyed e and prominent x-height doing the quiet work.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-gafata: Tilt Neon draws every line like a ruler, one width throughout, with a splayed c and short ascenders up top. Gafata, tall and wide-eyed, feels like a quiet reply.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Reading here means a high mean line and curves left open at the ends. Noto Sans Brahmi does that quiet work, while Tilt Neon's thread-stitched, constant-width tubes do the bold shouting.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Tilt Neon looks like twine pressed flat, one width all the way. Noto Sans Chorasmian lets its curves stop short and stays out of the way, so the loud heading leads.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-coptic: A splayed c terminal gives Tilt Neon its tube-like swagger, drawn at a single width. Noto Sans Coptic fills the middle of the line with open s and c, so the two sit together easily.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Tilt Neon draws a tube-like line at a single weight, while Noto Sans Cuneiform swells its lowercase like glass beads. Constant tubes against round beads: that is the whole charm.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Tilt Neon draws like a plotter pen, one line weight throughout. Noto Sans Duployan counters with a wide-mouthed a and oversized e, a loose, open foil to all that discipline.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-mende-kika: Stencil-cut tubes, loud and tall: that is Tilt Neon at a glance. It earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Mende Kikakui, a sans-serif, stands tall against the capitals.
